ANSWER: In a proportional-odds (ordered logit) regression of COVID-19 severity (ordinal 1–4, subject's max AESEV across their COVID-19 AEs) on BCG status (TRTGRP) and prior medical history (any MHORRES==2), controlling for patient interaction frequency (patients_seen, 3-level categorical), the **interaction OR (BCG × prior-medical-history) is 0.685, 95% CI [0.192, 2.441]** (interaction coefficient β = −0.3785, z = −0.584, p = 0.559). The CI includes 1.0, so there is **no statistically significant interaction** — the effect of BCG vaccination on COVID-19 severity does not differ meaningfully by prior-medical-history status in this sample (n=153 subjects with a documented, rated COVID AE).

## Primary model — priorMH = Option A (any MHORRES==2), n=153
Severity distribution: 1→56, 2→79, 3→11, 4→7. BCG×MH 4-cell counts: (Placebo,noMH)=29, (Placebo,MH)=47, (BCG,noMH)=26, (BCG,MH)=51.

Full coefficient table (proportional-odds logit; OR = exp(coef)):
| Term | coef | SE | z | p | OR | 95% CI (OR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCG | 0.3759 | 0.5031 | 0.747 | 0.455 | 1.456 | [0.543, 3.904] |
| MH_A | 0.5893 | 0.4524 | 1.303 | 0.193 | 1.803 | [0.743, 4.375] |
| **BCG×MH** | **−0.3785** | **0.6484** | **−0.584** | **0.559** | **0.685** | **[0.192, 2.441]** |
| PS 51–100 | −0.3280 | 0.3876 | −0.846 | 0.398 | 0.720 | [0.337, 1.540] |
| PS >100 | 1.0808 | 0.6571 | 1.645 | 0.100 | 2.947 | [0.813, 10.685] |
| θ 1/2 | −0.1492 | 0.3587 | −0.416 | 0.677 | — | — |
| θ 2/3 | 0.9720 | 0.1025 | 9.486 | <0.001 | — | — |
| θ 3/4 | 0.0446 | 0.3013 | 0.148 | 0.882 | — | — |
Model: llf=−156.20, df_model=5, df_resid=145, converged (5 Newton iters).

BCG × priorMH × severity cross-tab (cells = n):
| BCG \ MH | noMH | MH |
|---|---|---|
| Placebo | sev1=12, sev2=17, sev3=0, sev4=0 | sev1=15, sev2=27, sev3=3, sev4=2 |
| BCG | sev1=8, sev2=17, sev3=1, sev4=0 | sev1=21, sev2=18, sev3=7, sev4=5 |

## Sensitivity — priorMH = Option B (MHORRES==2 & MHCM=='Yes'), n=153
Interaction OR = **1.057, 95% CI [0.302, 3.704]** (β=0.0552, p=0.931); BCG OR=1.141, MH_B OR=0.983.
**Does it change materially?** The point estimate flips across the null (0.685 → 1.057) and the CI widens/shifts, but both are non-significant with overlapping, very wide CIs. The statistical conclusion is unchanged: no evidence of an interaction. So the interaction result is robust to the MH-coding choice (it is null either way), even though the point estimate is not stable.

## Proportional-odds assumption note
Levels 3 and 4 are sparse (n=11 and n=7). The proportional-odds model assumes the BCG, priorMH and their interaction shift every cumulative severity threshold by the same log-odds amount. With so few subjects at the top levels, the top-threshold (θ 3/4) estimate is imprecise (CI [−0.546, 0.635] in log-odds) and the interaction OR's CI is very wide — the null result is therefore partly a power limitation, not strong evidence of exactly no interaction. A non-proportional-odds (partial-PO) model could relax this but is under-powered at n=153 with a 4-way design.

## Assumptions / limitations
- Analysis unit = subject; outcome = subject's MAX AESEV across COVID-19-specific AE rows (AEPT contains COVID/SARS-CoV OR AEHLT='Coronavirus infections'); primary sample restricted to the 153 subjects with a documented, non-missing severity (44 all-NaN and 803 no-COVID subjects excluded).
- BCG := TRTGRP=='BCG' (500/500, consistent across DM/AE/MH). MH coded per approved Option A. patients_seen treated as 3-level categorical (ref 1-50).
- No R available; used Python statsmodels OrderedModel (distr='logit'). Interaction OR is the common (proportional-odds) odds ratio, identical at all thresholds.
